issue.title: [TECH DEBT] Remove SyncWrapper and finish the move from tornado to asyncio (3009.x)
issue.body:
### Description of the tech debt to be addressed

Salt started on tornado before asyncio existed in the standard library. Since then we vendored it (3006.x), moved to a current tornado (3007.x), and replaced most tornado coroutines with `async/await` (3008.x). What is left is mostly `salt.utils.asynchronous.SyncWrapper`, which lets sync code call async classes.

SyncWrapper creates a private event loop per instance and blocks on it. This is the source of many open bugs: unclosed-object warnings, nested-wrapper deadlocks, task leaks, and fork/GC cleanup problems. This issue tracks removing it for 3009.x.

The hard part is not tornado itself. It is the sync callers of async code. Use native async APIs and update their callers to await them. CLI and worker entry points can drive those coroutines with standard asyncio.

### Related bugs

Open:
- #70355 unclosed SyncWrapper for cls — mitigation #70370 merged to `3008.x` on 2026-10-28; it is not yet in the audited `master`
- #70175 unclosed object / SyncWrapper / publisher client warnings — related cleanup fixes #70206, #70261 and #70177 merged to `3008.x`; the issue remains open
- #69824 MWorker deadlock in `_store_job` -> `fire_event` — mitigation #70461 is open against `3008.x`
- #70353 minion deadlock in `zmq_ctx_term()` from a GC finalizer — fix #70415 is open against `3008.x`

Closed:
- #70169 SyncWrapper leaks asyncio tasks per call
- #69986 MWorker deadlock via nested SyncWrapper in `tcp.PublishServer.publish`
- #69637 Unclosed transport warning

Touch the same code but SyncWrapper is not the main cause: #70178, #70344, #70071, #66435, #69988.

### Current state (master, audited 2026-10-28)

Checked against `master` at `1ff0167934a4d528f9192f8467482b3bff1c8362`. Step 1 is 4/5 merged; #70369 is still open with passing CI and a required review. PR #70602 (open, not yet merged) converts `status.ping_master()` and scheduler dispatch to native coroutines, with awaited minion/proxy startup, CLI/worker dispatch, channel/event operations and TCP/ZeroMQ coverage. Other request callers still use SyncWrapper. Reference counts below exclude Python comments; call-site counts use the Python AST and include both sync and async callers.

SyncWrapper is created in only five places under `salt/`:

| Where | What it wraps |
|---|---|
| `utils/event.py` (2) | `SaltEvent.subscriber` and `SaltEvent.pusher` |
| `transport/tcp.py` | `PublishServer.pub_sock` |
| `channel/client.py` | `ReqChannel.factory` (23 direct factory call sites) |
| `utils/http.py` | `AsyncHTTPClient.fetch` |

Other numbers:

- 78 SyncWrapper references under `tests/`
- 20 files under `salt/` and 55 test files import tornado
- 18 `@gen.coroutine`: 3 in `AsyncReqMessageClient` (`transport/zeromq.py`), 15 in `netapi/rest_tornado`
- 57 `IOLoop` references and 4 `run_sync()` call sites under `salt/`
- Event API call sites under `salt/` (sync and async callers combined): `get_event()` 156, `fire_event()` 152

### Implementation PRs (updated 2026-10-29)

The PRs below are against `master` (#70604 is merged). The five new follow-ups are independent branches; they also merge together with #70602 without conflicts. Nothing here is marked complete until merged.

| PR | Issue | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| #70602 | #70643 | Native master ping and fully awaited scheduler/minion/proxy/CLI dispatch; shared result/executor utilities |
| #70603 | #70642 | Native shared authentication, per-attempt waiter ownership, error propagation, cancellation draining and awaited credential events |
| #70604 | - | Asyncio channel loops/locks, common transport factories for pool routing, and channel initialization/context-manager cleanup |
| #70605 | #70640 | With `master_async_mworker` on, TCP IPC publishing awaits delivery on the caller's loop (no nested SyncWrapper); with it off nothing changes |
| #70606 | #70644 | Await batch lifecycle events and the initial event connection, use presence notification, and drain batch/reconnect tasks before releasing shared channels |
| #70607 | #70645 | Serialize WebSocket requests, reuse connections, honor timeouts and await request-channel cleanup; real mutual TLS and Unix-socket coverage |
| #70608 | #70646 | Await WebSocket subscriber I/O and owned-task cleanup |
| #70609 | #70647 | Await WebSocket publisher startup, IPC delivery and shutdown |
| #70610 | #70648 | Await request-server cleanup before worker and router loop shutdown |
| #70611 | #70649 | Await native event sessions and minion request responses |
| #70639 | #70641 | Small `PublishServer` cleanups split out of #70605: unused `io_loop`, close the daemon's loop, a macOS test fix |

Local integration of the six PRs: **589 passed, 7 existing skips** on Python 3.11. After the final connection-race correction, **71 focused integration tests passed**, including all **52 batch tests**, maintenance-loop entry points, native TCP publishing, and WebSocket requests over TCP, mutual TLS and Unix sockets. Individual PRs record their focused tests and lint results. CI is still running; local results are not a claim that CI has completed. Master remains at the audited commit above, so the reference counts remain the master baseline rather than the unmerged implementation totals.

### Plan

Use independently reviewable implementation PRs. Related paths can advance while earlier removals await review; remove each wrapper only after its callers use native APIs and explicit cleanup.

**Step 1: Easy removals (low risk)**
- [x] Link the existing SyncWrapper bugs (see Related bugs)
- [ ] Remove the deprecated `zeromq.AsyncReqMessageClient` (nothing in `salt/` uses it). Also removes 3 `@gen.coroutine` and its tornado `Queue`/`Future` use. PR: #70369 (open; CI passing; review required)
- [x] Remove the deprecated `tcp.TCPReqClient`, and the `salt.transport.client` / `salt.transport.server` compat modules. PR: #70375 (merged to `master` 2026-10-27)
- [x] Remove the deprecated `tcp.TCPReqServer`. PR: #70376 (merged to `master` 2026-10-27)
- [x] Remove the deprecated `tcp.TCPPubClient` and `tcp.TCPPublishServer`. PR: #70377 (merged to `master` 2026-10-27)
- [x] Remove the deprecated `tcp.MessageClient` (about 270 lines), and add unit tests for `tcp.RequestClient`, which had none. PR: #70378 (merged to `master` 2026-10-27)

These all had `warn_until(3009, ...)` and nothing in `salt/` used them. Master is 3009.0, so the expired warnings also fail some unit tests in CI (`RAISE_DEPRECATIONS_RUNTIME_ERRORS=1`). Other expired `warn_until(3009)` calls (x509, etcd, vsphere, ...) are not part of this work.

**Step 2: Native async APIs and cleanup rules**
- [x] Use native `async def` / `await` for migrated I/O operations and update their actual callers. Run coroutines with standard asyncio at CLI and worker entry points; inline async jobs use the current running loop.
- [x] Record the working cleanup contract: explicit `close()` / `destroy()` or context managers; await async cleanup on the owning loop; closing one object only releases its own resources; the actual entry point owns the event loop lifecycle. Remove GC-time cleanup per migrated class only after caller cleanup and regression coverage are in place.

These rules guide the incremental implementation PRs and their tests. Keep `3008.x` compatibility fallbacks separate (#70261); #70122 remains relevant to the later removal of legacy finalizer cleanup on `master`.

**Step 3: Shared code (medium risk)**
- [ ] Follow up after reviewing #70606 and #70607: evaluate shared task registration and close coordination between batch and WebSocket clients. `cancel_tasks()` is already shared. Extract further helpers only where ownership, cancellation and completion contracts match; preserve existing method names, synchronous entry points and user-visible behavior, with regression coverage before refactoring.
- [ ] Migrate `status.ping_master()` as the first native async request caller. PR: #70602 (implemented; awaiting merge). Use `async def`, `AsyncReqChannel` with `async with`, and awaited requests, cleanup and failback events on the caller's loop. Await `Schedule.eval()`, `run_job()`, `_run_job()` and `handle_func()` through minion/proxy startup, periodic callbacks and management events. Keep loop startup at daemon, CLI and worker entry points; centralize result waiting and executor dispatch in existing utilities, and keep loader context across awaits. Coverage includes real local TCP/ZeroMQ requests, cancellation, timeouts, startup ordering and dispatch results.
- [ ] Finish migrating `channel/client.py` (`ReqChannel.factory`) callers and `fileclient.py`. #70603 and #70604 prepare native authentication/channel primitives and factory reuse; the synchronous request facade remains until its callers migrate.
- [ ] `utils/http.py`: `http.query()` uses SyncWrapper around tornado's `AsyncHTTPClient` for the default `tornado` backend. There are 16 direct `salt.utils.http.query()` call sites plus loader-dispatched callers, so decide first whether to keep the tornado HTTP backend or move to another one
- [ ] Remove `IOLoop` and `run_sync` usage (`aioloop()` and `current_ioloop()` helpers)
- [ ] Replace tornado `IOStream` with asyncio streams in the TCP IPC publisher (`_TCPPubServerPublisher`). `StreamClosedError` handling and the `ipc_write_buffer` cap need to move with it. After #70605.
- [ ] `cli/batch_async.py` (#70606) and `utils/channel.py` (#70604): implemented, awaiting merge.
- [ ] Update the test files that import tornado (55 at the audited master baseline). Channel and batch tests use native coroutines in #70604 and #70606.

**Step 4: Event bus and TCP transport (high risk)**
- [ ] `utils/event.py` and `transport/tcp.py`: #70605 removes the nested TCP IPC publisher wrapper. The outer event subscriber/pusher wrappers and their remaining callers still need migration.
- [ ] Minion event bus: `master_async_mworker` is a master option, so minions always use the original `PublishServer`. Add an option minions have and use the async publisher there. After #70605.
- [ ] Check the raw publisher in `cluster/consensus/peer.py`: no `ipc_write_buffer` cap and no send lock, so concurrent sends may interleave frames (not verified).
- [ ] Decide how `get_event()` / `fire_event()` behave when called from sync code and from inside a running loop
- [ ] Add stress tests for nested calls, fork, and shutdown
- [ ] Do this in small PRs; several related fixes are still open

**Step 5: Remove SyncWrapper (after steps 1-4)**
- [ ] Delete the class in `salt/utils/asynchronous.py` after its callers use native async APIs
- [ ] Remove SyncWrapper-only `async_methods` / `close_methods` metadata from `AsyncReqChannel` after its synchronous callers are migrated and SyncWrapper is removed (TODO in #70607)
- [ ] Remove the `__del__` safety nets that only existed for it
- [ ] Remove `master_async_mworker` and the original TCP IPC path once its default flips. The code is marked `REMOVE-WITH-FLAG(master_async_mworker)`.

**Out of scope unless we decide otherwise**
- Replacing `netapi/rest_tornado` (about 2.4k lines, 15 of the `@gen.coroutine`). Dropping tornado as a dependency entirely would need a rewrite of salt-api.

### Versions Report
N/A (tracking issue). Applies to 3008.x and master.

issue.title: [BUG] Byte conversion factors off by power of 10 in _parse_numbers() in modules/disk.py
issue.body:
**Description**

I was looking at [`salt/modules/disk.py`](https://github.com/saltstack/salt/blob/master/salt/modules/disk.py) and came across the following in the definition of [`_parse_numbers`](https://github.com/saltstack/salt/blob/master/salt/modules/disk.py#L32):

https://github.com/saltstack/salt/blob/93b640543c3d404d7b19d760f5f83a65ee936d67/salt/modules/disk.py#L42-L51

It seems to me that these are all off by a factor of 10: `K` should be `1E3`, not `10E3`, and so on.

This function seems to only be used by the `_iostat_aix()` function, so I don't know how large the impact is, or whether this may even be expected behavior on AIX platforms.

**Example**

I loaded the definition of `_parse_numbers` into an interpreter to play around with it. As noted, it seems to me that these values are off by a factor of 10:

```python
>>> float(_parse_numbers("1.0K"))
10000.0
# I would expect 1000.0

>>> float(_parse_numbers("32.8K"))
328000.0
# I would expect 32800.0
```

**Suggested fix**

Remove the extra `0` characters. I also recommend replacing the `E` with `e`, which helps distinguish the numbers from the `e` more easily (when written with a lowercase `e`, the current `10e3` value looks very suspect, especially next to the `K` suffix).

```python
postPrefixes = {
    "K": "1e3",
    "M": "1e6",
    "G": "1e9",
    "T": "1e12",
    "P": "1e15",
    "E": "1e18",
    "Z": "1e21",
    "Y": "1e24",
}
```

As a separate note, `postPrefixes` is IMO a poor name and should be renamed `unit_to_bytes` or `unit_suffixes` or something more clear, although that is unrelated to the issue at hand.

issue.title: [Tech-Debt] Avoid use of deprecated net-tools
issue.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The linux `net-tools` package has been deprecated since 2011, and provides commands including `arp`, `ifconfig`, `iptunnel`, `iwconfig`, `nameif`, `netstat`, and `route`.

Some salt modules make use of these commands, causing failures when they're not available (#57513).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Code should be rewritten, preferring first native python (e.g. `pyroute2`) then the `iproute2` tools (e.g. `ip`), then only falling back to `net-tools` if that's all that is available. If every supported platform has already migrated to `iproute2` then the fallback is not required.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Continue to depend on systems providing the `net-tools` package. This won't work forever.

**Additional context**
Replacement commands:

net-tools | iproute2
-- | --
arp | ip neighbor
ifconfig | ip addr, ip link, ip -stats
iptunnel | ip tunnel
iwconfig | iw
nameif | ip link
netstat | ss
route | ip route

issue.title: Async batch does not await its events and can release the shared channel too early
issue.body:
### Description of the tech debt to be addressed
Async batch (`salt/cli/batch_async.py`):
- Start and done events are fired without waiting for delivery, then a fixed 30 ms sleep runs before the shared event channel is released.
- Reconnection can be started without being awaited, and delayed batch tasks can outlive the shared channel.
- Unsubscribing one job ID passed as a string splits it into characters, so the real subscription stays registered.

### Proposed change
Await the batch events and finish batch-owned tasks before the shared channel is released. Keep the `close_safe()` name and await its cleanup. Unsubscribe the whole job ID.

issue.title: [TECH DEBT] etcd support depends on etcd3-py, which has had no release since 2019
issue.body:
### Description of the tech debt to be addressed, include links and screenshots

Salt's etcd support (`salt.utils.etcd_util`, the `etcd` execution and state modules, and the `etcd3` cache) uses [etcd3-py](https://github.com/Revolution1/etcd3-py), which has had no release since 0.1.6 in May 2019 and no commits since May 2022. With the v2 API removed in 3009, it is the only etcd client Salt uses.

[etcd3gw](https://pypi.org/project/etcd3gw/) is maintained by OpenStack (2.7.0 was released in June 2026), talks to the same etcd v3 HTTP gateway and is synchronous, so it can replace etcd3-py behind `EtcdClientV3` without changing its public methods. It can't authenticate with a user name and password yet. I've proposed that upstream in https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/etcd3gw/+/1013860 ([Launchpad bug 1970750](https://bugs.launchpad.net/python-etcd3gw/+bug/1970750)), and Salt can carry a small subclass until it is released.

Porting the code turned up contract problems on master that are worth fixing while 3009 is open:

- Recursive operations use a plain key prefix. On master with etcd3-py, `rm("/app", recurse=True)` also deleted `/application` and `/app-old`. `tree`, `ls`, `get(..., recurse=True)` and recursive watches match those keys too.
- `read()`, and so `get`, `tree` and `ls`, return `None` for every error, so an unreachable etcd, bad credentials or a permission error look like a missing key to the module, sdb and pillar callers.
- `etcd.watch` with its default `timeout=0` returns `None` immediately.
- The `etcd.set`, `etcd.rm` and `etcd.directory` states write with `test=True`. `etcd.set` rewrites keys that already have the right value and can't create a key without a profile (it reports "No profile found"). `etcd.rm` reports "Unable to remove key" with `result: True`. `wait_rm` drops `recurse`. `etcd.directory` raises on etcd v3.
- A user name without a password, or a client certificate without its key, is silently ignored, and a client certificate without `etcd.ca` uses plain HTTP.

I'll open a PR against master for both.

### Versions Report

master at 2a0d5484df, etcd 3.6.5, etcd3-py 0.1.6.

issue.title: Windows: file.replace needs 3 runs
issue.body:
### Description of Issue
When modifying a file with file.replace on Windows, the first 2 runs modify the file and the 3rd run reports the files as "Clean". On Linux, this already happens at the 2nd run, as expected.

### Setup
Here's a simple SLS file to reproduce the issue:
```
{%- if grains['kernel'] == 'Windows' %}
  {%- set drive = 'C:' %}
{%- else %}
  {%- set drive = '' %}
{%- endif %}

create_file:
  file.managed:
    - name: {{ drive }}/tmp/pg_hba.conf
    - makedirs: True

allow_ipv4:
  file.replace:
    - name: {{ drive }}/tmp/pg_hba.conf
    - repl: host    all             all             0.0.0.0/0               md5
    - pattern: ^host\s+all\s+all\s+0\.0\.0\.0/0\s+md5.*
    - append_if_not_found: True
    - require:
      - file: create_file

allow_ipv6:
  file.replace:
    - name: {{ drive }}/tmp/pg_hba.conf
    - repl: host    all             all             ::/0                    md5
    - pattern: ^host\s+all\s+all\s+::/0\s+md5.*
    - append_if_not_found: True
    - require:
      - file: create_file
```

Apply above state to a Linux and a Windows minion multiple times. Windows will need 3 tries to show that everything is in desired state, while Linux needs 2.

issue.title: [Bug]: Add python.run and python.script execution and state modules
issue.body:
### What happened?

Description

Salt's packages bundle a "onedir" build of Python that is separate from whatever Python (if any) is installed on the target system. Today there's no built-in way to run a snippet of Python code or a Python script using that specific interpreter — cmd.run/cmd.script will happily execute python/python3, but which interpreter that resolves to depends entirely on the system's PATH.

This request adds a new execution module, python, with:

- python.run — run a snippet of Python code (-c) or raw interpreter arguments (e.g. -m module), using the exact same Python interpreter (sys.executable) that is running the Salt minion/master.
- python.script — download a Python script (via cp.cache_file/cp.get_template, same flow as cmd.script) and execute it with that same interpreter, rather than relying on the script's shebang line, executable bit, or PATH.

And a paired state module, python, with run and script states mirroring cmd.run/cmd.script's conventions, so this can be used declaratively in SLS files.

Motivation

Onedir packaging means the Python actually executing Salt code is often not the same interpreter a user would get from python3 on PATH. Being able to target Salt's own interpreter directly is useful for automation that needs to guarantee consistent Python behavior/version regardless of what's installed on the system.

Proposed API

salt '*' python.run command="print('hello world')"
salt '*' python.run args="-m json.tool foo.json"
salt '*' python.script salt://scripts/runme.py 'arg1 arg2'

write-marker-file:
  python.run:
    - name: open('/tmp/salt-marker', 'w').close()

run-my-script:
  python.script:
    - source: salt://scripts/runme.py
    - args: arg1 arg2

### Type of salt install

Official deb

### Major version

3007.x

### What supported OS are you seeing the problem on? Can select multiple. (If bug appears on an unsupported OS, please open a GitHub Discussion instead)

almalinux-8

### salt --versions-report output

```shell
3009
```
